For the modeled peak cooling load of 1,400 tons (4.9 MW in Figure 14c), the estimated total capital costs for chiller units ranged from approximately $1.5 million to $2.36 million. • Circulating Pumps: Capital cost for pumps was estimated using a correlation of $1,000 per kW of pump power (Oh et al. 2025b). The required pump capacity, based on the modeled peak power consumption of 52.7 kW, resulted in a total capital cost of $52,700. • Cooling Towers: A cost of $300/ton was used based on current market estimates for water-cooled cooling towers with similar thermal and flow specifications of a case study (P2S Engineering 2011). For a maximum rejected thermal load of 1,646.4 tons through cooling towers, the capital cost of the cooling tower was estimated at $493,920. • Piping Infrastructure: Piping costs were estimated using reference values reported in the Los Angeles Valley College Central Plant case study (P2S Engineering 2011). For a representative 500-ft length of 18-inch-diameter pipe (sized to accommodate flow rates exceeding 5,250 GPM while maintaining velocity below 2.5 m/s), the installed cost was estimated at $699/ft, resulting in a total piping cost of $349,500. This estimate includes labor, material, and insulation. • Initial Water Fill: Initial water cost was estimated based on the cooling towers’ peak flow rate (4,083 GPM). Assuming a conservative fill duration of 5 hours, representing the time required to fully charge the loop volume at peak flow, the total water volume was estimated at approximately 1.22 million gallons (4,637 m³).
